  [inst_3 : CommMonoid M] (f : M → R),
  (∀ (a : M), 0 ≤ f a) →
    f 1 ≤ 1 → (∀ (x y : M), f (x * y) ≤ f x * f y) → ∀ (s : Finset ι) (g : ι → M), f (∏ i ∈ s, g i) ≤ ∏ i ∈ s, f (g i)
items.informal_description: Let $M$ be a commutative monoid and $f : M \to R$ a function satisfying three conditions: (1) non-negativity ($f(a) \geq 0$ for all $a \in M$), (2) unit bound ($f(1) \leq 1$), and (3) submultiplicativity ($f(xy) \leq f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y \in M$). For any finite set $s$ and function $g : s \to M$, the inequality $f\left(\prod_{i \in s} g(i)\right) \leq \prod_{i \in s} f(g(i))$ holds.

items.informal_name: Product Degrees Inequality in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {ι : Type u_3} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → MvPolynomial σ R},
  (∏ i ∈ s, f i).degrees ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, (f i).degrees
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $ of indices and a family of multivariate polynomials $ f_i $ over $ \sigma $ with coefficients in a commutative semiring $ R $, the multiset of variables in the product $ \prod_{i \in s} f_i $ is less than or equal to the sum of the variable multisets of each $ f_i $. This partial order denotes submultiset inclusion, meaning every variable in the product's multiset appears with multiplicity no greater than its total multiplicity in the summed multisets.

items.informal_name: Schwartz-Zippel Lemma: Root Bound via Supremum of Exponent Ratios
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [inst_2 : DecidableEq R] {n : ℕ} {p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R},
  p ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (S : Fin n → Finset R),
      ↑{x ∈ Fintype.piFinset fun i => S i | (MvPolynomial.eval x) p = 0}.card / ∏ i, ↑(S i).card ≤
        p.support.sup fun s => ∑ i, ↑(s i) / ↑(S i).card
items.informal_description: For any non-zero multivariate polynomial $ p $ in $ n $ variables over a commutative semiring $ R $, and for any finite subsets $ S_i \subseteq R $ for each variable, the ratio of the number of roots of $ p $ in the product set $ S_1 \times \cdots \times S_n $ to the product of the cardinalities $ \prod_{i=1}^n |S_i| $ is at most the supremum over all monomials $ s $ in the support of $ p $ of the sum $ \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{s_i}{|S_i|} $, where $ s_i $ denotes the exponent of the $ i $-th variable in the monomial $ s $.
